summary: The required, quantum and breadth courses must be letter graded with a B+ or better (PHYSICS 290 and 294 are offered only S/NC and count with an S), and quantum and breadth courses must be taken for at least 3 units. The research and colloquium courses are not held to a letter grade, and the 135-unit total counts every graduate course. Your 3.3 GPA, the two breadth areas outside your own research, the proposal, presentation, teaching, qualifying exam, oral exam and dissertation are checked by hand.
